title: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
focus: Kuka asks who a person is. Kuka sinä olet? — Minä olen Anna.
targetSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Who are you?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Kuka asks who a person is. In a neutral question, put kuka first: Kuka sinä olet? (“Who are you?”). Do not add -ko/-kö. The complete question means “Who are you”.
requiredSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
exercises.targetSkill: Kuka: asking and answering about one person

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking a person's or thing's identity + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question asking a person's or thing's identity
parts.formation: Kuka is the basic singular human question pronoun.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the singular you-form olet: ole- + -t.

optionFeedback.Kuka sinä olet?: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. A pronoun stands in place of a name or noun. Kuka asks who a person is. In a neutral question, put kuka first: Kuka sinä olet? (“Who are you?”). Do not add -ko/-kö. The complete question means “Who are you”.
optionFeedback.Mikä sinä olet?: Mikä identifies or selects one countable thing. The requested question is “Kuka sinä olet?”
optionFeedback.Missä sinä olet?: Missä asks for a location: where. The requested question is “Kuka sinä olet?”

exercises.prompt: Answer “Kuka minä olen?”: choose “You are Mikko.” Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Answer from your own point of view: sinä olet (“you are”) in the question becomes minä olen (“I am”) in your reply. Hän on stays hän on when both speakers mean the same other person. Minä and sinä may be omitted with olen and olet; keep hän when referring to another person. In a role game, Kuka minä olen? (“Who am I?”) receives Sinä olet… (“You are…”), because the reply addresses the original speaker. The complete reply means “You are Mikko”.
requiredSkills: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
exercises.targetSkill: Kuka: asking and answering about one person
